Sources

The 947 sources cited on this site. Each person's page footnotes the exact entry and page. Under each source is what we hold of it ourselves: an archived copy of the page or record (so the evidence survives if the website it came from goes away), the index rows or the transcription, and, for US federal records, the image. “Original at” links go to the archive or index where the record can be seen.

  • Marriage (1911) and baptism of Elvīra Sirlaka (1912) at Rīga St Martin's, Torņakalns. Rīga St Martin's Lutheran parish registers (1911–1912) & My Life and Times, ¶6. LVVA Raduraksti & Elvīra Danenberga memoir. Cited for Emma Smukule.
    Archived copy held: 2 files (doc, eml).
    Transcription we hold (1)
    The first two years of my life were spent in Torņukalns (Tower Hill), a suburb of Rīga. My father, Mārtinš Sirlaks, and my mother Emma Smukulis were both born about 8 km from each other: my mother in Vecrauna (Old Rauna) and my father in Jaunrauna (New Rauna). … At first they both worked in menial jobs, but then my father opened a tavern while mother stayed at home as a housewife. When WWI started in 1914, they left Rīga to escape the anticipated disruptions and disturbances of war and went to Cēsis

IS.—(Special.)— Adam Pershbaker, prominent early settler of Coos County, died suddenly, at Prosper last night at the age of 79 years. He came to the county in iS71, was the first,merchant in the Coquille Valley, owned the famous Black Sand mines and townsite of Randolph during the gold rush in the ’70s and built the Prosper sawmill in 1888. His es- i tate of $250,000 is left to two daughters, Mrs. S. W. Fdhy, of Prosper, and Mrs, Andrew Muir, of Oakland, Cal. The funeral will.be held here Tuesday.
    Translation: COOS EARLY SETTLER DEAD / Adam Pershbaker Stricken Suddenly at Age of 79. BANDON, Or., Feb. 18.—(Special.)—Adam Pershbaker, prominent early settler of Coos County, died suddenly at Prosper last night at the age of 79 years. He came to the county in 1871, was the first merchant in the Coquille Valley, owned the famous Black Sand mines and townsite of Randolph during the gold rush in the '70s and built the Prosper sawmill in 1888. His estate of $250,000 is left to two daughters, Mrs. S. W. Fahy, of Prosper, and Mrs. Andrew Muir, of Oakland, Cal. The funeral will be held here Tuesday.

    Dr. Wolfgang Schubach, internist Dr. Wolfgang Schubach practiced internal medicine. His office was at 29001 Cedar Rd., Beachwood.; Cancer was diagnosed two months ago and Dr. Schubach died Saturday at his home in Beachwood. He was 64. Dr. Schubach was bom in Wiesbaden, Germany, and came to the United States in 1957. He had been graduated from medical school in Bonn. He worked two years at Suburban Community Hospital and then took his internship and residency at Huron Road Hospital where he was named to the medical staff. Dr. Schubach’s hobby was photography and he had taken several prizes in shows at the Jewish Community Center. He is survived by his wife, Dr. Margaret Schubach; sons Wolfhart and Dieter; daughter Gisella DeDomenico; stepsons Dr. Robert Cendo and Richard W. Cendo; a great-granddaughter and a brother. Memorial services will be at 7:30 p.m. tomorrow at his home, 27500 Cedar Rd.

    Translation: KILLED BY AN ENGINE / Rev. C. Alderson Meets Death on Track at Albany. ALBANY, Or., Oct. 12.—Rev. C. Alderson, a retired pioneer Methodist minister, whose home was at Salem, was instantly killed this morning by the engine of a freight train. He was hurled from a trestle 30 feet down and forward to the rocks of Pennywinkle Creek, this city. His skull was crushed by the fall. ... The Rev. Christopher Alderson was born in Yorkshire, England, September 11, 1827, and came to the United States in 1850. He crossed the plains in 1852, and settled in Oregon. He was married to Mary C. Royal, August 13, 1862, and she survives him. ... He is survived by his widow, Mrs. Mary C. Alderson, two sons, Professor W. C. Alderson, of St. Johns, and W. S. Alderson, of Portland; four daughters, Mrs. Margaret Burkhart, of Albany, and Mrs. Anna Pearson, of Ashland, Or.; Miss Edith R. and Miss Lola Alderson, residing with their mother in Salem. The funeral services will be held in the Sunnyside Methodist Episcopal Church, East Yamhill and Thirty-fifth streets, Monday afternoon at 2 o'clock.

    .MRS. MARY ALDEKSON, PIONEER OF OREGON, DIES Mrs. Mary Royal Alderson, 80, died early Sunday at her home at No. 1208 Belmont street of injuries she suffered at midnight Friday when she fell to the floor In her room. Physicians said she did not recover consciousness after her fall. Mrs. Alderson was the widow of the late Rev. Christopher P. Alderson, pioneer circuit riding minister of the Methodist Episcopal church. She was born in Cook county, 111., January 26, 1842, and crossed the plains with her parents, Mr. and Mrs. Charles Royal, In 1852, settling at Astoria. The Royal family moved later to a donation land claim near Gresham, taking with them the daughter, Mary, who grew up there and met and married the Rev. Alderson, spending the next 40 years with him In his pastorates throughout Western Oregon and Washington. She is survived by one son, W. S. Alderson, and four daughters, two of whom. Miss Edith Alderson and Mrs. Lois Huggins, live Dr Portland. Two other daughters live In Albany, Mrs. Anna Pearson and Mrs. Marguerite Burkhart. A brother, William Royal of Elma, Wash., also survives. Funeral services will be held nt 30 a. m. Wednesday at Sunnyslde Methodist church, where Mrs. Alderson had her membership at the time of her death. Interment will be at the Lincoln Park Memorial cemetery.

A brother, William Royal of Elma, Wash., also survives. Funeral services will be held at 10 a. m. Wednesday at Sunnyside Methodist church, where Mrs. Alderson had her membership at the time of her death. Interment will be at the Lincoln Park Memorial cemetery.

    Translation: Phil. G. Barnhart Killed by Lightning. One of the severest electrical storms ever known in this section occurred last evening about dark, and was followed by rain throughout the night. Mr. Phil. G. Barnhart, living at Northwood, while engaged at work about the cream separator at his home was struck by a bolt of lightning, and almost instantly killed, dying before Dr. Mulder, who was summoned, could reach him. Mr. Barnhart was an old resident, having lived here more than twenty years, and was the father of a large family. He was an estimable citizen, honored and respected, and his sudden and unfortunate death will be a shock to his many friends. A curious incident is that some six years ago, during a much less severe electrical storm than that of last evening, Mr. Barnhart's barn was struck by lightning, set on fire, and it and its contents totally destroyed.

    The first two years of my life were spent in Torņukalns (Tower Hill), a suburb of Rīga. My father, Mārtinš Sirlaks, and my mother Emma Smukulis were both born about 8 km from each other … At first they both worked in menial jobs, but then my father opened a tavern while mother stayed at home as a housewife. When WWI started in 1914, they left Rīga to escape the anticipated disruptions and disturbances of war and went to Cēsis

    Izvadot māc. A. Briedim, 13. oktobrī Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumā apglabāja 9. oktobrī 85 g. vecumā mirušo Emmu Sirlaku. Viņa pārmaiņus dzīvojusi gan ASV, kur paliek divas meitas ar ģimenēm, gan – pēdējos gados – Toronto pie meitas Mirdzas Gailītes un znota – matēmatikas skolotāja Friča Gailīša, kas mira pērngada septembrī. Emma Sirlaka nedaudzu gadu laikā pārcieta vairākas smagas operācijas, amputācijā zaudējot vispirms vienu, bet pirms diviem gadiem arī otru kāju.
    Translation: With Rev. A. Briedis officiating, on 13 October in the Latvian section of York Cemetery was buried Emma Sirlaka, who died on 9 October aged 85. She had lived by turns in the USA, where two daughters with their families remain, and – in the last years – in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law, the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis, who died last September. Within a few years Emma Sirlaka underwent several severe operations, first losing one leg to amputation and two years ago the other.
    Izvadot māc. A. Briedim, 13. oktobrī Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumā apglabāja 9. oktobrī 85 g. vecumā mirušo Emmu Sirlaku. Viņa pārmaiņus dzīvojusi gan ASV, kur paliek divas meitas ar ģimenēm, gan - pēdējos gados - Toronto pie meitas Mirdzas Gailītes un znota - matēmatikas skolotāja Friča Gailīša, kas mira pērngada septembrī. Emma Sirlaka nedaudzu gadu laikā pārcieta vairākas smagas operācijas, amputācijā zaudējot vispirms vienu, bet pirms diviem gadiem arī otru kāju.
    Translation: With Rev. A. Briedis officiating, Emma Sirlaka, who died on 9 October aged 85, was buried on 13 October in the Latvian section of York Cemetery. She had lived alternately in the USA, where two daughters survive with their families, and, in recent years, in Toronto with her daughter Mirdza Gailīte and son-in-law, the mathematics teacher Fricis Gailītis, who died last September. Within a few years Emma Sirlaka underwent several serious operations, losing first one leg and, two years ago, the other to amputation.

    Transcriptions we hold (2)
    F. Gailītis Latvijā strādāja par skolotāju kopš 1929.g. Pēc ieceļošanas Kanādā, nostrādājis līguma gadu "Hydro" sabiedrības būvēs, viņš bija viens no pirmajiem latviešu skolotājiem Kanādā, kas pēc papildstudijām un pārbaudījumu izturēšanas ieguva vidusskolas skolotāja tiesības. Nelaiķis piederēja studentu kosporācijai Fraternitas Academica un Toronto pēc Sv. Andreja draudzes nodibināšanas vairākus gadus bija tās kasieris.
    Translation: F. Gailītis worked as a teacher in Latvia from 1929. After arriving in Canada, having worked a contract year on the construction works of the "Hydro" company, he was one of the first Latvian teachers in Canada who, after further study and passing examinations, obtained high-school teacher's qualifications. The deceased belonged to the student corporation Fraternitas Academica and, after the founding of St. Andrew's congregation in Toronto, was its treasurer for several years.
    Ar sirdstrieku 23. septembrī miris ilggadīgais skolotājs, matēmatiķis 64 g.v. Fricis Gailītis, kas pirms pieciem gadiem pārdzīvoja sirdslēkmi un pavadīja slimnīcā pie divi mēneši. Otrdienas rītā viņšs savā darba vietā vidusskolā pēkšņi jutās ļoti slikti, daži kollēgas viņu nogādāja mājā. No turienes slimnieku ar ambulances auto noveda "Sunnybrook" slimnīcā. Kad ārsts paskaidroja, ka krize pārvarēta, un slimnieka dzīves biedre pēc kāda laika devās mājās, stāvoklis pēkšņi mainījās, un mājās viņu drīz sasniedza telefoniska vēsts, ka vīrs miris. … Aizgājēju 27. septembrī uz Jorkas kapsētas latviešu nodalījumu izvadīja māc. Ā. Čops, kas arī vadīja piemiņas svētbrīdi "Rosar" apbedīšanas mājā iepriekšējā vakarā. Nelaiķim paliek Toronto dzīves biedre Mirdza un brālis Latvijā.
    Translation: On 23 September long-time teacher, mathematician, 64 years old, Fricis Gailītis died of a heart attack; five years ago he had survived a heart attack and spent about two months in hospital. On Tuesday morning at his workplace, a high school, he suddenly felt very unwell, some colleagues took him home. From there the patient was taken by ambulance to "Sunnybrook" hospital. When the doctor explained that the crisis was over, and the patient's wife after some time went home, his condition suddenly changed, and at home the telephone news soon reached her that her husband had died. … On 27 September the deceased was escorted to the Latvian section of York Cemetery by Rev. Ā. Čops, who also led the memorial service at the "Rosar" funeral home the evening before. The deceased leaves in Toronto his wife Mirdza, and a brother in Latvia.

    Transcription we hold (1)
    Par „pionieri“ savā nozarē Kanādā, laikam būs jāuzskata LU matēmatikas maģistrs Fricis Gailītis, kas šopavasar pēc Ontario College of Education nobeigšanas ieguvis vidusskolas skolotāja tiesības un rudenī stāsies darbā. F. Gailītim aiz muguras 16 gadu skolotāja prakse Latvijā un arī Vācijā viņš darbojies par skolotāju latviešu ģimnāzijā Hanavā. Ieceļojis Kanādā 1948. g., viņš pirmās gaitas te sāka ar lāpstu un kapli, bet pēc līguma saistību izpildīšanas pievērsās namdara arodam. Arī to viņš darīja pamatīgi, piecus gadus apmeklēdams Toronto centrālā technikuma vakarskolu … Bet rudenī viņš atkal būs „baltās apkaklītes strādnieks“ un mācīs matēmatiku „Danforth Technical School“ audzēkņiem.
    Translation: As the "pioneer" in his field in Canada one will probably have to regard Fricis Gailītis, Master of Mathematics of the University of Latvia, who this spring, after finishing the Ontario College of Education, obtained secondary-school teacher's qualifications and will start work in the autumn. F. Gailītis has behind him 16 years of teaching practice in Latvia, and in Germany too he worked as a teacher at the Latvian gymnasium in Hanau. Having come to Canada in 1948, he began here with shovel and hoe, but after his contract obligations were fulfilled he turned to the carpenter's trade. He did that thoroughly too, attending for five years the evening school of the Toronto Central Technical School … But in the autumn he will again be a "white-collar worker" and will teach mathematics to the pupils of Danforth Technical School.

    Translation: 5000 Relatives in Missouri: Harry Norman, a St. Louis newspaper man, was in Hannibal last night returning from the funeral of his grandmother, Mrs. Emma Jane Nolen, of Monroe City, who died there Thursday. Mrs. Nolen was a pioneer of Northeast Missouri and had lived in Monroe county for nearly three-fourths of a century. With many of her relatives in Culpeper county, Virginia, she emigrated to Missouri when a child and it is probable that she is related to 5,000 persons in this section of the State principally around Monroe City, Paris and Stoutsville. She was the mother of ten children, six of whom survive her, the grandmother of twenty-six and the great-grandmother of twenty-three, twenty-one of whom survive. The surviving children are: J. H. Nolen, of Jefferson City, Deputy State Labor Commissioner; F. M. Nolen, of Paris, Sheriff of Monroe county; Oliver T. Nolen of Iola, Kas.; Ambrose J. Nolen, Melvin P. Nolen and Mrs. Mary E. Norman, of Monroe City. Mrs. Nolen, whose maiden name was Yowell, was a member of the Christian Church and the widow of John L. Nolen, a native of Hardin county, Kentucky. Her husband also was a pioneer settler of Northeast Missouri. He was one of the first shippers of live stock over the Hannibal and St. Joseph railroad.

    Agr. A. Danenbergs no Ohaio stāstīja par savu pieredzi Amerikas lopkopībā un piensaimniecībā. Referents, kas strādā par piena pārraugu un vada savu piensaimniecības farmu, norādīja uz visai šauro speciālizēšanos tikai vienā virzienā šinī zemē: piensaimniecībā, graudkopībā, gaļas lopu audzēšanā utt, uz ko spiežot visai dārgās saimniekošanas metodes, nepieciešamās mašīnas, dārgais darba spēks uc. apstākļi.
    Translation: Agronomist A. Danenbergs from Ohio told of his experience in American livestock and dairy farming. The speaker, who works as a milk tester and runs his own dairy farm, pointed to the very narrow specialisation in only one direction in this country: dairying, grain growing, beef cattle etc., to which the very expensive farming methods, the necessary machines, expensive labour and other circumstances push one.

    Auto sadursmē miris agr. Arvids Danenbergs. 19. februārī Mičiganā automašīnu sadursmē miris agronoms Arvids Danenbergs. Pēc slimnīcas ārstu atzinuma viņš miris ar sirdstrieku, bet nav zināms, vai tā notikusi pirms jeb arī pēc sadursmes. Arī A. Danenberga sieva Elvira sadursmē ievainota un nogādāta slimnīcā. Arvids Danenbergs dzimis 1913. gada 17. janvārī Tukumā, Latvijā ieguvis agronoma gradu, Vācijā maģistra gradu lauksaimniecībā. [...] Par vīra pēkšņo aiziešanu mūžībā skumst vēl slimnīcā dzīvesbiedre Elvira, meitas, dēli ar ģimenēm, brālis Žanis Latvijā, piederīgie un jo kupls draugu pulks. V. Boķis
    Translation: Agronomist Arvids Danenbergs killed in a car collision. On 19 February in Michigan, in a collision of cars, agronomist Arvids Danenbergs died. According to the hospital doctors he died of a heart attack, but it is not known whether it happened before or after the collision. A. Danenbergs's wife Elvira was also injured in the collision and taken to hospital. Arvids Danenbergs was born on 17 January 1913 at Tukums; in Latvia he obtained an agronomist's degree, in Germany a master's degree in agriculture. [...] The sudden passing of her husband is mourned by his wife Elvira, still in hospital, daughters, sons with families, brother Žanis in Latvia, relatives and a very large circle of friends. V. Boķis

    17. novembrī savā dzīves vietā pēkšņi mirusi 84 g. vecā Berta Buša, dzim. Ludviga. Dzimusi 1908. g. 16. jūnijā, Dundagas pag., lībiešu pēcnācēja, kristīta un iesvētīta Mazirbes baznīcā. Pēc vidusskolas beigšanas mācījusies LU farmacijas fakultātē. [...] Piederēja vienības “Ausma” saimei. Viņu izvadīja 23. novembrī māc. J. Mednis, guldīja zemes klēpī Vudlavna kapsētā, latviešu nodalījumā, blakus jau agrāk mirušajam dzīvesbiedram. Kapos atvadījās no draudzes un Bēru fonda — B. Maine, no Mežvidu pārvaldes — E. Avots, E. Danenberga no vienības “Ausma”, A. Tālberga un J. Rumberga no Akadēmiskās kopas, no Bībeles stundu dalībniekiem — Z. Golta, no draugiem — māc. V. Fricsone.
    Translation: On 17 November, suddenly at her home, died Berta Buša, née Ludviga, aged 84. Born 16 June 1908 in Dundaga parish, a descendant of Livonians, baptised and confirmed in Mazirbe church. After secondary school she studied at the pharmacy faculty of the University of Latvia. [...] She belonged to the Ausma association. She was conducted on 23 November by Rev. J. Mednis and laid to rest in Woodlawn cemetery, in the Latvian section, beside her husband who had died earlier. At the graveside farewell was said for the congregation and the funeral fund by B. Maine, for the Mežvidi administration by E. Avots, for the association Ausma by E. Danenberga, for the Academic Circle by A. Tālberga and J. Rumberga, for the Bible-study participants by Z. Golta, for friends by Rev. V. Fricsone.

    Manā uztverē vajadzētu atrast visā ASV 1000 personu vai organizāciju, kam nekādu grūtību nesagādātu ziedot 1000 dol. Tas dotu 1 milj. dol. Bet nekas nenotika — mafijas vara vēl vienmēr turpinās un neviens nejūtas drošs ne dienu, ne nakti, ne mājā, ne uz ielas. Tādēļ priecājos par fonda nodibināšanu un piesaku savu 1000 dol. ziedojumu (esmu pensionārs) cerībā, ka mērķis tiks pacelts no 1/2 milj. uz 1 milj. dol. savākšanu.” agr. A. DANENBERGS
    Translation: In my view one should find 1000 persons or organisations in the whole USA for whom donating 1000 dollars would be no hardship. That would give 1 million dollars. But nothing happened — the mafia's power still continues and nobody feels safe day or night, at home or in the street. So I am glad of the founding of the fund and pledge my 1000 dollar donation (I am a pensioner), hoping the target will be raised from 1/2 million to collecting 1 million dollars. agr. A. DANENBERGS

    Tālāk agr. A. Danenbergs no Ohio stāstīja par savu pieredzi Amerikas lopkopībā un piensaimniecībā. Referents, kas strādā par piena pārraugu un vada savu piensaimniecības farmu, norādīja uz visai šauro speciālizēšanos tikai vienā virzienā šinī zemē: piensaimniecībā, graudkopībā, gaļas lopu audzēšanā u.t.t., uz ko spiežot dārgās saimniekošanas metodes, nepieciešamās mašīnas, dārgais darba spēks u.c. apstākļi. Vispārējos vilcienos A. Danenbergs pieskārās piena ra- [p. 4:] žībai, barošanai, šejienes ganāmpulkiem un deva mazu salīdzinājuma ainu mūsu dzimtenes piensaimniecībā brīvvalsts laikos un Savienotajās valstīs.
    Translation: Next agr. A. Danenbergs from Ohio told of his experience in American livestock and dairy farming. The speaker, who works as a milk tester and runs his own dairy farm, pointed to the very narrow specialisation in only one direction in this country: dairying, grain growing, beef cattle etc., to which expensive farming methods, the necessary machines, expensive labour and other conditions push one. In general outline A. Danenbergs touched on milk yield, feeding, local herds, and gave a small comparative picture of dairying in our homeland in the free-state era and in the United States.

    1944.g. Arvīds ar sievu, 2 gadus vecu dēlu Pēteri un sievas māti Emmu Širlaku dodas bēgļu gaitās uz Vāciju.
    Translation: In 1944 Arvīds, his wife, their two-year-old son Pēteris and his wife's mother Emma Širlaka fled as refugees to Germany.
    Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs, dzimis 1913.g. 17. janvārī Tukuma apriņķa Stūrmuižas pagastā. Pēc 2.Jelgavas valsts ģimnāzijas beigšanas studē Lauksaimniecības Akadēmijā Jelgavā, ko beidz ar agronoma grādu. Strādā Talsu agronomiskā birojā. 1941.g. no Sv. Jāņa baznīcas Cēsīs uzsāk kopīgu ģimenes dzīvi ar farmaceiti Elvīru Širlaku. 1944.g. Arvīds ar sievu, 2 gadus vecu dēlu Pēteri un sievas māti Emmu Širlaku dodas bēgļu gaitās uz Vāciju. Tur turpina izglītību Štutgartes—Hohenheimas agrikultūras augstkolā, kur iegūst mākstera grādu agronomijā. 1949.g. izceļo uz ASV. … Miris pēkšņā nāvē auto katastrofā 1996. g. 19. februārī, atstājot sievu Elvīru, trīs bērnus — Pēteri, Kalvi, Līgu, 3 mazbērnus ASV, brāli Žani un vairākus radus Latvijā. Pārpelnots un pelnu urna nosūtīta uz Latviju.
    Translation: Arvīds Fricis Danenbergs, born 17 January 1913 in Stūrmuiža parish, Tukums district. After finishing the 2nd Jelgava State Gymnasium he studied at the Agricultural Academy in Jelgava, graduating as an agronomist. He worked at the Talsi agronomy bureau. In 1941, from St John's church in Cēsis, he began family life with the pharmacist Elvīra Širlaka [sic]. In 1944 Arvīds, his wife, their two-year-old son Pēteris and his wife's mother Emma Širlaka fled as refugees to Germany. There he continued his studies at the Stuttgart-Hohenheim agricultural college, earning a master's degree in agronomy. In 1949 he emigrated to the USA. … Died suddenly in a car accident on 19 February 1996, survived by his wife Elvīra, three children (Pēteris, Kalvis, Līga), 3 grandchildren in the USA, his brother Žanis and several relatives in Latvia. Cremated; the urn was sent to Latvia.
    1944.g. Arvīds ar sievu, 2 gadus vecu dēlu Pēteri un sievas māti Emmu Širlaku dodas bēgļu gaitās uz Vāciju. Tur turpina izglītību Štutgartes—Hohenheimas agrikultūras augstkolā, kur iegūst māstera gradu agronomijā.
    Translation: In 1944 Arvīds with his wife, 2-year-old son Pēteris, and mother-in-law Emma Sirlaka went into exile to Germany. There he continued his education at the Stuttgart-Hohenheim agricultural college, where he earned a master's degree in agronomy.
    Tur turpina izglītību Štutgartes—Hohenheimas agrikultūras augstkolā, kur iegūst māstera grādu agronomijā.
    Strādā Talsu agronomiskā birojā. … Papa remained in Talsi, where he had his workplace.

    Elvīrai Danenbergai, dzim. Sirlaka, piepildījās 75 mūža gadi. Dzimusi 1912. g. 9. janv. Rīgā. Skolas gadus pavadījusi Cēsīs. 1941. g. beigusi LU Ķīmijas fakultātes Farmacijas nod. ar maģistra gradu. Strādājusi Rīgā un vairākās provinces aptiekās. ASV apmetusies Ohio, un kopā ar vīru agr. Arvīdu uzaudzināja 2 dēlus un meitu. Strādāja par farmaceiti Tiffin Ohio. Pārceļoties uz Mičigenu, dzīvo savā farmā Gaŗezera tuvumā. DV apvienībai Latvijas ciemā pievienojās 1982. g. un ir pašreizējās Vanadžu kopas vad. Jubilāri 9. janvārī sveica DV apv. vadība, Vanadžu kopas vadība un Ciema vanadzes. E.O.
    Translation: Elvīra Danenberga, née Sirlaka, completed 75 years of life. Born 9 January 1912 in Rīga. She spent her school years in Cēsis. In 1941 she graduated from the Pharmacy Department of the Faculty of Chemistry of the University of Latvia with a master's degree. She worked in Rīga and in several provincial pharmacies. In the USA she settled in Ohio, and together with her husband agronomist Arvīds raised 2 sons and a daughter. She worked as a pharmacist in Tiffin, Ohio. Moving to Michigan, she lives on her own farm near Garezers. She joined the DV association in Latvijas ciems in 1982 and is the present head of the Vanadzes circle. On 9 January the jubilarian was congratulated by the DV association board, the Vanadzes circle board and the Ciems vanadzes. E.O.
    Elvīrai Danenbergai, dzim. Sirlaka, piepildījās 75 mūža gadi. Dzimusi 1912. g. 9. janv. Rīgā. In 1941 graduated from the Pharmacy Section of the Chemistry Faculty of the University of Latvia with a master's degree. Worked in Rīga and several provincial pharmacies. In the USA settled in Ohio and with her husband, the agronomist Arvīds, raised 2 sons and a daughter. Worked as a pharmacist in Tiffin, Ohio. Moving to Michigan, she lives on her farm near Garezers.

    Klīvlenda (J. L.) — Latviešu neklātienes skolas skolēni pulcējās 2 nedēļu vasaras nometnē Danenbergu lauku īpašumā pie Tifinas, Ohaijo. Nodarbības vadīja skolot. A. Bankovics un V. Dindone. [...] „Lai vientuļi izkaisītie latviešu bērni varētu pabūt kādu laiciņu kopā, Danenbergs nodeva bez atlīdzības mūsu lietošanā savu saimniecību un ar ģimeni bija piepalīdzīgs dažādos nometnes darbos. Mūsu izrīcībai bija klavieres, latviešu skaņu plates un grāmatas, bet vaļas brīžos dārzā mielojamies pie jāņogām, ķiršiem un zemenēm", piezīmē skolot. V. Dindone. [...] Uzvedumus noskatījās ciemiņi no Tifinas un netālās Klīvlendas.
    Translation: Cleveland (J. L.) — Pupils of the Latvian correspondence school gathered for a 2-week summer camp on the Danenbergs' farm near Tiffin, Ohio. Classes were led by teachers A. Bankovics and V. Dindone. [...] "So that the lonely, scattered Latvian children could be together for a while, Danenbergs placed his farm at our disposal free of charge and with his family helped with the various camp tasks. We had a piano, Latvian records and books, and in our free moments we feasted in the garden on currants, cherries and strawberries," notes teacher V. Dindone. [...] The performances were watched by guests from Tiffin and nearby Cleveland.

    No mums šķīrusies Mirdza Gailīte (dzirn. [sic: dzim.] Sirlaks) dzimusi 1916. gada 17. janvāri Vidzemes skaistajā pilsētā Cēsis. … Pēc Otrā pasaules kara liktenis ģimeni aizveda uz Kanādu. … Pēc vīra aiziešanas mūžībā kādu laiku dzīvoja Detroitas apkaimē West Bloomfield savā dzīvoklī. Viņa 1990. gada sākumā iestājās Detroitas Daugavas Vanagu apvienībā … Mirdzas divas māsas arī dzīvoja West Bloomfield un Garezera (Long Lake) apkaimē. Pēc aiziešanas pensijā Mirdza Gailīte atgriezās Vindzorā, Kanādā … Mirdza Gailīte aizgāja mūžībā pēkšņi 2010. gada 5. jūlijā. Viņu izvadīja 10. jūlijā no Anderson Funeral Home Vindzorā. Nelaiķe guldīta smilšu kalniņā Toronto.
    Translation: Mirdza Gailīte (née Sirlaks) has left us. Born 17 January 1916 in the beautiful Vidzeme town of Cēsis. … After the Second World War fate took the family to Canada. … After her husband's death she lived for a while in her apartment in West Bloomfield, near Detroit. In early 1990 she joined the Detroit Daugavas Vanagi branch … Mirdza's two sisters also lived in West Bloomfield and near Garezers (Long Lake). After retiring Mirdza Gailīte returned to Windsor, Canada … She died suddenly on 5 July 2010. The funeral was on 10 July from Anderson Funeral Home, Windsor. She was laid to rest in Toronto.

    Arvids F. Danenbergs Jan. 17, 1913-Feb. 19, 1996 CASSOPOLIS — Memorial services for Arvids F. Danenbergs, 83, of 56882 Point Road, .who died at 4:43 p.m. Monday in Lee Memorial Hospital, Dowagiac, of injuries suffered in a two-car accident at Dutch Settlement and Decatur roads in Penn Township, will be announced later. Friends may call from 4 to 7 p.m. Friday at Connelly Funeral Home. Cremation will follow. He was bom Jan. 17, 1913, in Auce, Latvia, Germany. In 1941, in Cesis, Latvia, he married Elvira Sirlaks. She survives with a daughter, Liga Schubach of Milwaukee; two sons, Peter Danenberg'of Altadena, Calif., and Kalvis Danenbergs of Midland, Ohio;- three grandchildren; and a brother, Zanis of Latvia, He was a member of the Local Latvian Community Gar- ezers, Three Rivers, and studied agriculture and science.

    Dec. 21, 1916 – Feb. 8, 2018 At Edith's request, there will be no service for Edith Evelyn Leslie, 101, formerly of Bandon. She died Feb. 8, 2018 at home in Eugene. The descendant of pioneers in Coos County, Edith loved spending most of her retirement living on the family ranch near Bandon. She was born Dec. 21, 1916, in Oakland, Calif., to Andrew Robertson Muir and Ruby Edith (Pershbaker) Muir. An only child, she was raised in the countryside near Los Gatos where her favorite playmates were her beloved dogs, cats, ducks and geese. After graduating from a preparatory school for young ladies, Edith became one of the first women to enter Stanford University, where she studied art. She earned a liberal arts degree from the University of Washington in 1937 and her teacher's credential from the University of California at Berkeley in 1938. She married Williamar Leslie, a fellow Stanford student from Mountain View, Calif., June 2, 1941, in the Stanford Memorial Chapel. They made their first home in Wilmington, Dela., and Williamar commuted to his job as a market analyst on Wall Street until a position with U.S. Steel in San Francisco, Calif., brought them back to the West Coast. Edith and Williamar lived in Berkeley, Calif., where Edith taught English to recent immigrants. They raised three children, Lael, Lorin, and Lann, in a home filled with parrots, iguanas, geese, geckos, lizards and Edith's art work. When Williamar retired in 1969, they decided to build a house on the Coquille River ranch that Edith's grandfather Adam Pershbaker, a mill owner and the founder of Prosper, had purchased shortly before she was born.

    Translation: KALAMAZOO. On 19 February, in Lee Memorial hospital in the city of Dowagiac, Michigan, the agronomist Arvīds Danenbergs died after a collision between two cars. … His wife Elvīra, riding with him, was injured … Arvīds Danenbergs was born 17 January 1913 in Tukums. Danenbergs was held on 4 March at 'Saulgrieži', Garezers … farewells were spoken by the deceased's wife's sister Mirdza Gailīte and daughters Līga Šūbacha (Schubach) and Ilze Bērziņa. … Mourned by his wife Elvīra (still in hospital), daughters, sons with families, brother Žanis in Latvia
    KALAMAZŪ. (Vm.) — 19. februārī „Lee Memoral" slimnīcā „Dawagiac" pilsētā Mičiganā, pēc divu automašīnu sadursmes miris agronoms Arvīds Danenbergs. Pēc slimnīcas ārstu atzinuma, viņš miris ar sirdstrieku, bet palika nenoskaidrots, vai tā sākusies pirms sadursmes un izsaukusi nelaimes gadījumu, jeb arī pēc sadursmes. [...] Arvīds Danenbergs dzimis 1913. gada 17. janvārī Tukumā. Latvijā ieguvis agronoma gradu, bet Vācijā maģistra gradu lauksaimniecībā. [...] Vēl pēdējās dienās paspēja nodot Latvijas zemessargu atbalstam 1000 dol. ziedojumu. Pēc kremācijas A. Danenbergam veltīts piemiņas brīdis notika 4. martā Garezera „Saulgriežos", DV apvienības ciemā „Latvija" izkārtojumā. Aizlūgumu un svētības vārdus teica prāv. Jānis Turks, Baibas Dumpes korāļu pavadījumā. Pēc noslēgumā nodziedātās Latvijas himnas, aizgājēju atcerējās un atvadu vārdus teica mirušā sievas māsa Mirdza Gailīte, meitas: Līga Šūbacha (Schubach) un Ilze Bērziņa, Auseklis Elksnis runāja Agronomu biedrības, Kalamazū Latviešu biedrības un DV apvienības Kalamazū vārdā, no atbalsta saņēmējiem Latvijā pateicās Vilis Miķelsons, Garezera pārvaldes — Gundars Strautnieks, Virsnieku apvienības — Albins Dravnieks un DV apvienības ciemā „Latvija" — Juris Krievs.
    Translation: KALAMAZOO (Vm.) — On 19 February in 'Lee Memorial' hospital in the city of 'Dowagiac', Michigan, after a collision of two cars, agronomist Arvīds Danenbergs died. According to the hospital doctors he died of a heart attack, but it remained unclear whether it began before the collision and caused the accident, or after the collision. [...] Arvīds Danenbergs was born on 17 January 1913 at Tukums. He obtained his agronomist's degree in Latvia and a master's degree in agriculture in Germany. [...] In his very last days he managed to hand over a donation of 1000 dollars in support of the Latvian Zemessardze. After the cremation a memorial hour for A. Danenbergs was held on 4 March at Garezers 'Saulgrieži', in the arrangement of the DV association in the village 'Latvija'. Prayer and blessing words were spoken by Rev. Jānis Turks, accompanied by Baiba Dumpe's choir. After the Latvian anthem sung at the close, the departed was remembered and farewell words said by the deceased's wife's sister Mirdza Gailīte, daughters Līga Šūbacha (Schubach) and Ilze Bērziņa; Auseklis Elksnis spoke for the Agronomists' Society, the Kalamazoo Latvian Society and the DV association of Kalamazoo; for the aid recipients in Latvia Vilis Miķelsons gave thanks; for the Garezers administration Gundars Strautnieks; for the Officers' Association Albins Dravnieks; and for the DV association in the village 'Latvija' Juris Krievs.
    brālis Žanis Latvijā

    Agr. A. Danenbergs apskatīja lielo un mazo farmu ienesību, salīdzinot kolchozu sistēmu tagadējā Latvijā un Amerikas lielsaimniecības, kurām pavērtas pavisam citas darba iespējas materiālā un ražošanas ziņā. Viņa atzinums bija, ka lielās saimniecības var ražot lētāk, maksāt lielākas algas strādniekiem, bet mazās saimniecības var eksistēt tikai tad, ja nav jānodarbina algots darba spēks.
    Translation: Agr. A. Danenbergs reviewed the profitability of large and small farms, comparing the kolkhoz system of present-day Latvia with American large farms, which have quite different working possibilities in terms of materials and production. His conclusion was that large farms can produce more cheaply and pay workers higher wages, but small farms can exist only if no hired labour has to be employed.

    When WWI started in 1914, they left Rīga … and went to Cēsis
    then my father opened a tavern while mother stayed at home as a housewife
    We applied to go to the US, which we entered in July, 1949. … The ship landed in Boston

    The first two years of my life were spent in Torņukalns (Tower Hill), a suburb of Rīga.

    At first we lived in a rented house in the Vinterkalns area, several km outside of Cēsis. … Mirdza was born in this house.
    Here Ilze was born in 1945 and one year later, the twins Līga and Kalvis.
    In the first year, I lived with father’s sister Anna.
